entries.title: The Western Plaguelands
body: Before the Third War this was beautiful forested farmland stretching from the capital to the Eastweald. Hearthglen was the seat of its government, and Andorhal distributed the grain of all Lordaeron's northern provinces.

It was here that the plague took hold. Now the farmlands and forests are dying, the pines browning, the trees pulsing with tumour-like growths. The Scourge holds Andorhal and Caer Darrow, the Scarlet Crusade holds Hearthglen, and the Argent Dawn wages a guerrilla war against both from the edges.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Western Plaguelands (History, Scourging of Lordaeron)

entries.title: Chillwind Camp
body: A small Argent Dawn camp at the southern edge of the Plaguelands, the last safe place for Alliance travellers entering them. It has only a few soldiers and specialists, and relies on mercenaries to carry out raids and guerrilla attacks on Andorhal and the plague cauldrons.
It was from here, years ago, that Darion Mograine set out with volunteers to free his father's soul from Naxxramas.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Chillwind Camp (The Ashbringer, World of Warcraft)

entries.title: The Bulwark
body: The Forsaken's last bastion against the Scourge on the border with Tirisfal, held with the Argent Dawn. The yellow-grey plague mist of the Plaguelands hangs over it. During the Scourging of Lordaeron, Uther gathered the survivors of the fallen capital here.

entries.title: Andorhal
body: One of the largest cities of northern Lordaeron and one of the oldest holy sites of the Church of the Holy Light. It was the distribution centre for the north's grain, so Kel'Thuzad's cult poisoned its granaries, and the plague spread from here to every village on the King's Road. Arthas and Jaina came to investigate and found it burning; Arthas hunted Kel'Thuzad down north of the city and killed him.

Later, Uther and his paladins made Andorhal their headquarters against the Scourge, until Arthas returned for Kel'Thuzad's remains and overran it. Its clocks all stopped at three o'clock. The last defenders set the city ablaze so the Scourge could raise no more of them. The lich Araj the Summoner rules its ruins.

entries.title: The Plague Cauldrons
body: To spread the plague as widely as possible, the Cult of the Damned set four huge cauldrons in the fields of the four largest farms around Andorhal, each guarded by a Cauldron Lord and constantly spewing disease into the air.
Gahrron's Withering, in the east, was once Del Gahrron's farm, Gahrron's Quickening; the others are Felstone Field, Dalson's Tears and the Writhing Haunt.

entries.title: Felstone Field
body: Once a farm that fed the region, now overrun by the Scourge and its cauldron, guarded by Cauldron Lord Bilemaw. Scarlet Crusaders come here too, and kill living and undead alike. In the house in the corner of the field, Janice Felstone still waits.

entries.title: Dalson's Tears
body: Once Dalson's Orchard, in the middle of the Plaguelands, now poisoned by a cauldron under Cauldron Lord Malvinious. The family never left: Mrs. Dalson wanders the property as a skeleton, and Farmer Dalson, now a ghoul, is locked in the outhouse.

entries.title: The Writhing Haunt
body: A farm just east of Andorhal, now overrun by the Scourge and poisoned by a cauldron under Cauldron Lord Razarch. A lone dwarf, Mulgris Deepriver, hides in one of its houses.

entries.title: Hearthglen
body: A walled town and old principality of Lordaeron, ruled from Mardenholde Keep, whose walls never fell to the orcs. Tirion Fordring was its lord, until he was stripped of his title and exiled for defending an orc. His son Taelan later succeeded him.

In the Third War it was sent poisoned grain from Andorhal. Arthas tracked the shipment and arrived just as the people had eaten their bread; he killed the infected before the plague could spread and held off the Scourge until Uther came. Ironically, the future Lich King saved Hearthglen. After the fall of the capital the Silver Hand took refuge here. Now it is a stronghold of the Scarlet Crusade, Taelan among its commanders.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Hearthglen (Second War, Of Blood and Honor, Third War, Ashbringer)

entries.title: Northridge Lumber Camp
body: A lumber mill near Hearthglen run by the Scarlet Crusade. Both the Alliance and the Horde know how much the Crusade depends on its lumber. Before the war, Nathaniel Dumah's family ran it.

entries.title: Sorrow Hill and Uther's Tomb
body: Sorrow Hill was Andorhal's cemetery, for rich and poor alike. When the plague came the graves multiplied, hastily dug and poorly marked, until the townsfolk stopped burying their dead and burned them in a pit to keep them from rising. Now the cauldrons have raised the hill's dead anyway.

Uther the Lightbringer died on the road outside Andorhal, carrying King Terenas's ashes in a funeral procession when Arthas met him. His soldiers took back his body, and the last act of the townsfolk before abandoning Andorhal was to build him a great tomb on the hill. High Priest Thel'danis keeps it, the only bastion of the Light in a dying land.

entries.title: Caer Darrow
body: An island fortress in Darrowmere Lake, one of the most storied places of old Lordaeron. It held an ancient high elven runestone, until the Horde sacked it in the Second War and carved the stone into the Altars of Storms. When Uther sailed to comfort the survivors, Alterac's privateers ambushed him, and the captured sailors revealed Alterac's treachery to the Alliance. The lake saw many naval battles in that war.
Afterwards the Barov family restored the keep and ruled a wide domain from it, Brill, Southshore and Tarren Mill among it. The Fordrings often visited. Beneath it now lies the Scholomance.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Caer Darrow (Ancient history, Second War, The Barovs and Scholomance)

entries.title: Highlord Taelan Fordring
body: The son of Tirion Fordring. When Tirion was exiled, his wife Karandra told the boy his father was dead, and took him to a false grave where he buried the toy hammer Tirion had given him, and the memory of his father with it.

Taelan became a paladin, sheltered the Silver Hand at Hearthglen when Lordaeron fell, and after Alexandros Mograine's death joined the Scarlet Crusade, rising high in its ranks while blind to the worst of what it does. He is lord of Mardenholde Keep now, as his father once was.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Taelan Fordring (introduction, Of Blood and Honor, The Ashbringer)

entries.title: Chromie
body: A bronze dragon in the guise of a gnome, who has come to Andorhal because something is wrong with time there. The Scourge seems to be trying to alter the city's past, and temporal parasites have infested its silos.

entries.title: Araj the Summoner
body: A lich who led the Scourge's Undead Ravagers against Hearthglen in the Third War, and now rules the ruins of Andorhal with an army of ghouls, skeletons, banshees and abominations.

entries.title: House Barov
body: In the years before the Third War, the Barovs grew depressed, greedy and bitter. To keep their fortune and their land long past their natural lives, they made a deal with Kel'Thuzad. The keep of Caer Darrow secretly became the Scholomance, a school of necromancy.

Within six months it was decrepit and full of dark things; the cult's acolytes learned their craft there and used the family's servants to test the plague. Just before Uther was due to visit, a disease bred in the Scholomance swept the island, and no one survived. Its victims wander as ghosts. The cult then killed the Barovs.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Caer Darrow (The Barovs and Scholomance)

entries.title: The Plague Cauldrons and the Grain
body: Before his assault on human civilisation, the Lich King poured his plague into portable cauldrons, and Kel'Thuzad's cultists hid them in villages they controlled across the north. The plan worked perfectly: village after village was infected, and those who caught the plague died and rose as the Lich King's slaves.
Andorhal was the key. Its grain went everywhere, so the cult poisoned it and ringed it with four great cauldrons. As Lordaeron collapsed, the land itself began to die.

entries.title: The Death of Uther
body: After the fall of the capital, Uther and the Silver Hand held Andorhal and guarded Kel'Thuzad's tomb nearby. On the dreadlord Tichondrius's orders, Arthas came for the necromancer's remains, which he needed a vessel to carry.

He killed Gavinrad, Ballador and Sage Truthbearer, and their soldiers. On the road outside the city he found Uther leading a small funeral procession, carrying King Terenas's urn. The teacher and his student fought, and Arthas killed Uther, took his father's urn, and poured out the ashes to carry Kel'Thuzad's remains in it.
